content.text:
**Finding restored to: Compliant — no redline, no counterparty comment.**

I withdrew the "(90)" insertion. The verifier is right on both counts: the edit was typographic rather than substantive, and "For ninety days" is already legally unambiguous, so raising it under WARRANTY would have spent negotiating capital and risked reopening a warranty package that already favours us. If the numeral convention matters, it belongs in a non-substantive drafting clean-up pass, not a playbook deviation.

Basis for compliance:

- **§19.1** — professional and workmanlike, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus an untimed conformity warranty for Services and Deliverables.
- **§19.2** — 90 days from the later of delivery or acceptance for each Deliverable; since "Deliverable" (§1.4) is bespoke work product, not licensed software, that matches our preferred services-side period. The software/hosted element conforms **throughout the subscription term**, exceeding our 12-month software preference.
- **§19.3** — compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution, open-source protection.
- **§19.4** — re-perform/repair/replace at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees on failure to cure, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; **§6.2** adds acceptance-stage correction and refund rights.
- **§19.5** — mutual, implied-warranties-only disclaimer with an express carve-out, so it does not swallow the express warranties.

Recorded for the file, not raised: the malicious-code warranty covers only code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" — market-standard, and acceptable against the non-exclusive remedy stack.

Note on the deterministic check: the ≥90-day period test fails only because the period is written in words rather than numerals. That is a false negative, and I have deliberately not manufactured a deviation to satisfy it.
